subject: chem
title: Carboxylic Acids and Derivatives
subtitle: Carboxylic acids, acyl chlorides, esters and amides.
concept: Carboxylic acids (–COOH) are weak acids; they react with bases, carbonates and alcohols.
Acyl chlorides are more reactive than carboxylic acids; they react vigorously with water, alcohols, and amines without needing a catalyst.
Esters and amides are formed by substitution of the OH or Cl of the carbonyl-containing group.

notes.heading: Carboxylic Acids
items: Weak acids: partially dissociate in water. pKa ~4–5 for simple carboxylic acids.
React with Na₂CO₃/NaHCO₃: RCOOH + Na₂CO₃ → RCOONa + H₂O + CO₂ (effervescence — test for carboxylic acid; aldehydes/ketones do not react with Na₂CO₃).
Esterification: RCOOH + R'OH ⇌ RCOOR' + H₂O (H₂SO₄ catalyst, reversible).

notes.heading: Acyl Chlorides
items: Prepared from carboxylic acid + PCl₅ (or SOCl₂).
More reactive than carboxylic acids (better leaving group Cl⁻ vs OH⁻).
With water: RCOCl + H₂O → RCOOH + HCl (steamy fumes of HCl).
With alcohol: RCOCl + R'OH → RCOOR' + HCl (ester formed, no catalyst needed, fast).
With ammonia: RCOCl + 2NH₃ → RCONH₂ + NH₄Cl (primary amide).
With primary amine: RCOCl + RNH₂ → RCONHR + HCl (secondary amide).

notes.heading: Esters
items: Hydrolysis (acid): RCOOR' + H₂O ⇌ RCOOH + R'OH (reversible; H⁺ catalyst).
Hydrolysis (base/saponification): RCOOR' + NaOH → RCOONa + R'OH (irreversible → drives to completion).
Polyesters: e.g. Terylene (PET) from benzene-1,4-dicarboxylic acid + ethane-1,2-diol.
Biodiesel: transesterification of vegetable oil triglycerides with methanol.

notes.heading: Amides
items: Polyamides: nylon — condensation polymer; e.g. nylon-6,6 from hexanediamine + hexanedioic acid.
Hydrolysis of amide: heat with HCl(aq) → carboxylic acid + ammonium salt; or NaOH(aq) → carboxylate + amine.

definitions.body: A carboxylic acid derivative with –COCl group; more reactive than the parent acid due to the better leaving group (Cl⁻).
Base hydrolysis of an ester using NaOH; irreversible — produces a carboxylate salt and an alcohol.
A polymer formed by repeated condensation reactions, with loss of a small molecule (usually H₂O or HCl) at each step.

workedExamples.q: Describe how to make ethyl ethanoate from ethanoyl chloride and explain why no catalyst is needed.

steps.text: Cl⁻ is a much better leaving group than OH⁻ — the reaction proceeds rapidly without needing acid catalysis.
Vigorous reaction; steamy fumes of HCl produced; ester formed (fruity smell).

mistakes: Confusing acid hydrolysis (reversible) with base hydrolysis (irreversible) of esters.
Using Na₂CO₃ to test for aldehydes/ketones — only carboxylic acids give CO₂ effervescence with Na₂CO₃.
Forgetting that acyl chlorides react violently with water (not like carboxylic acids which need a catalyst for esterification).
tips: Acyl chloride reactions are faster and don't need a catalyst — use when you need to make an ester or amide efficiently.
Saponification (NaOH hydrolysis) is irreversible — produces RCOONa (sodium salt), not carboxylic acid.
Polyester or polyamide? Diol + diacid → polyester (ester link –COO–); diamine + diacid → polyamide (amide link –CONH–).

flashcards.q: What is the test for a carboxylic acid?
flashcards.a: Add Na₂CO₃ (or NaHCO₃): carboxylic acid gives effervescence (CO₂). Aldehydes and ketones do not react.

flashcards.q: What is the product of ethanoyl chloride reacting with ethanol?
Why is base hydrolysis of an ester irreversible?
flashcards.a: NaOH is consumed; the carboxylate salt (RCOO⁻) formed cannot reverse the reaction under these conditions.
Base (NaOH) hydrolysis of an ester → carboxylate salt + alcohol. Used industrially to make soap from fats.

flashcards.q: What monomers are used to make nylon-6,6?
flashcards.a: Hexane-1,6-diamine + hexanedioic acid (condensation polymerisation with loss of H₂O).

flashcards.q: How does an acyl chloride react with ammonia?
flashcards.a: RCOCl + 2NH₃ → RCONH₂ (amide) + NH₄Cl. One NH₃ reacts; the other neutralises HCl.

questions.q: Which reagent distinguishes a carboxylic acid from an aldehyde?
questions.exp: Na₂CO₃ reacts with carboxylic acids (CO₂ effervescence); aldehydes do not react with Na₂CO₃.

questions.q: What is the product of base hydrolysis (NaOH) of ethyl ethanoate?
Which is more reactive toward nucleophilic addition-elimination?
questions.exp: Acyl chlorides (–COCl) are more reactive than carboxylic acids or esters because Cl⁻ is a much better leaving group.

questions.q: What small molecule is lost in forming a polyamide?
questions.exp: Polyamide (nylon) is formed by condensation of diamine and diacid — water is lost at each step.

questions.q: Hydrolysis of an ester using HCl(aq) is:
questions.exp: Acid hydrolysis of esters is reversible (equilibrium); base hydrolysis (saponification) is irreversible.

recall: Describe reactions of carboxylic acids with Na₂CO₃, alcohols and LiAlH₄.
Explain why acyl chlorides are more reactive than carboxylic acids.
Describe the preparation of an ester from an acyl chloride.
Compare acid and base hydrolysis of esters.
Describe the formation of nylon-6,6 as a condensation polymer.
